subject: Intermittent upload failures from Aurelia air-gapped gateway — MTU/SG/NAT triage
messages:
From: Tom Everett <tom.everett@aurelia-health.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@aurelia-health.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Uploads failing via air-gapped gateway (intermittent fragmentation)

Markus,

We started seeing intermittent failures when our on-prem EHR system POSTs ~2.5MB payloads to Redwood Private running in our air-gapped VPC. The requests sometimes succeed but more often we get TCP retransmits and application-level checksum errors. Our ops team suspects MTU/fragmentation between our gateway appliance and Redwood's front-end. This is blocking our integration tests for tomorrow's scheduled cutover.

I've attached a small pcapture and an edge router config excerpt. Key facts:
- Failures appear when payloads exceed ~1500 bytes after TLS overhead (roughly 1400 payload).
- Gateway is an appliance in Aurelia's datacenter; we use GRE to the Redwood edge.
- Our NAT range is 10.250.0.0/22, ephemeral ports 32768-61000.

Can your team confirm whether the Redwood edge is mss-clamping, or if security groups are dropping fragmented packets? We're in a compliance-sensitive environment, so please keep compliance@cc'd.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Everett
Lead Infrastructure Engineer
Aurelia Health

Attachments: packet_capture_20270517.pcap (pcap), edge_config_excerpt.txt (text)

From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Tom Everett <tom.everett@aurelia-health.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, compliance@aurelia-health.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Uploads failing via air-gapped gateway (intermittent fragmentation)

Tom — thanks for the capture and config. I've looped in Dev (networking) and Marissa (customer success). We'll triage immediately.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) Dev will review the pcap for signs of fragmentation/ICMP "Fragmentation needed" or MSS mismatch.
2) We'll validate the SGs on the ingress edge for AED (airgap-edge-demarc) to ensure fragments aren't dropped by strict stateful inspection.
3) If we need to, we can temporarily enable an MSS clamp at the GRE/edge termination (suggested clamp: 1220) and test again.

Marissa: please propose a 30-minute test window today or tomorrow where Aurelia can run repeat POSTs while we toggle clamp.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, Tom Everett <tom.everett@aurelia-health.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Uploads failing via air-gapped gateway (intermittent fragmentation)

Tom — I pulled the pcap. Observations:
- I see many TCP retransmits and out-of-order segments; I also see ICMP "Fragmentation needed" (Type 3 Code 4) from an intermediate hop around the GRE tunnel egress.
- Packet lengths suggest PMTU between the gateway and Redwood edge is ~1476 for tunneled traffic. After TLS and GRE overhead the usable MSS is ~1380, so large POSTs exceed that.
- I don't see explicit RSTs from security groups, but fragments are being generated and the endpoint sometimes drops reassembled packets.

Immediate remediation I recommend:
- Apply an MSS clamp of 1220 on the GRE termination on Redwood edge for traffic from Aurelia's source range (10.250.0.0/22). This avoids fragmentation across the path while preserving TCP performance.
- Ensure our edge allows fragmented packets and that conntrack timeout is sufficient for large transfers. Suggest increasing conntrack timeout for related sessions to 120s during the test window.

I've attached a short config excerpt for the clamp and my test log.

Attachments: mss-test-results.log (text)

I can apply the clamp in a non-disruptive fashion during a short window and then revert if there's any regression. Markus, if approved I'll schedule and notify Aurelia.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Tom Everett <tom.everett@aurelia-health.com>, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Uploads failing via air-gapped gateway (intermittent fragmentation)

Tom — thanks for confirming availability. Aurelia, can you do a 30-minute window today at 14:00 PT? We'll:
- Dev will enable the MSS clamp on the GRE termination.
- Evelyn (SRE) will monitor metrics and conntrack table; we will also capture a fresh pcap.
- You should run a repeat of the failing POST sequence and share timestamps.

Quick ask for Aurelia ops before the window: please confirm whether the appliance does any inline deep packet inspection (DPI) that could drop fragments, and share any appliance software/version info. That will help us rule out middleboxes.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: Tom Everett <tom.everett@aurelia-health.com>, markus.klein@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Uploads failing via air-gapped gateway (intermittent fragmentation)

Follow-up with results from today's window (14:00 PT):
- We applied MSS clamp 1220 on GRE termination at 13:55, increased conntrack timeout for related flows to 120s, and captured traffic for 14:00–14:30.
- Aurelia ran 120 POSTs during the window; success rate improved from ~64% to 99.2%. Failures observed were small and matched client-side timeouts rather than TCP retransmit drop.
- Fresh pcap shows no more ICMP "Fragmentation needed" on the path; fragmentation is avoided and reassembly issues stopped.
- We also found two security group rules on the edge that had a tight "allow established only" behavior for UDP and fragmented TCP — we've relaxed that rule to allow fragments for the source range to avoid future drops.

Next steps/recommendations:
1) Persist the MSS clamp for Aurelia's source range for the next 7 days while they complete cutover tests.
2) Confirm appliance DPI settings on Aurelia side; if DPI is enabled, advise configuring it to reassemble fragments or increase MTU on the GRE hop if possible.
3) I'll open a short change request to modify the SG rule description so future audits show purpose and rollback steps.

Tom — can you confirm whether Aurelia wants the clamp persisted or prefers a short-term approach? Also send appliance software/version per Marissa's ask so we can note it in the incident.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: packet_capture_20270520_after.pcap (pcap), edge_config_after.txt (text)
